summary: A 1933 L-4 cab in the Sespe Wilderness, Los Padres NF: staffed round the clock in WWII, later a condor monitoring station, reached by a 3.5-mile trail.

facts.design: L-4 14 x 14 ft cab with catwalk on a 20 ft H-braced tower
facts.wartime: Staffed 24 hours a day in World War II; ground cabin added for the off-duty observer during 12-hour shifts
facts.condor_monitoring: Used as a condor monitoring station; the lookout is near the Condor Sanctuary

visit.trail_note: About 3.5 miles from Thorn Meadows Campground through the Sespe Wilderness; no motorized use

events.note: Register gives 1933 for the L-4 cab
Trail being built up to the new lookout, per an August 1934 newspaper item
Forest Service ran a Ground Observer Corps post out of the lookout
Austin Mack observer May to November; a 1958 item calls it his fourth year

notes_for_editor: Built year 1933 comes from the register only; the August 1934 newspaper item calls the lookout new, which fits. 'Still standing' is the Forest Service's own line on an undated trail page. No source read says whether the cab is open to visitors or climbable, so access level and climbability are left out of facts. The Ojai Valley News hiking column returned HTTP 429 and was not read. Record name, coordinates and elevation match the register; no corrections proposed. The weebly page spells it Thorne; the register and Forest Service use Thorn. No staffing after 1958 was found.
